issues.claim: audit_md: "years after the firm's last archived use (18 August 2018)"; rescue.json likely_cause: "Wayback snapshots show the firm's own site on www.nord-demaio.com up to 18 Aug 2018"
issues.problem: Wrong date. The Wayback CDX list cited in founder_md (http://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=nord-demaio.com&output=json) shows the firm's own page captured well after 18 Aug 2018 with the identical content digest (JCJGHO76V52MUDY4QFHNZAP4JZHSTB3M) on 2018-09-05, 2018-10-06, 2018-10-08 and 2019-01-26, so 18 Aug 2018 is not the firm's last archived use. The last capture of the firm's own page is 26 January 2019. The spam content does still appear by 17 Nov 2019, so the finding itself stands.
issues.fix: Change both places to "the firm's last archived use (26 January 2019)". With that date the "about six years" gap before the 27 March 2025 re-registration is accurate, so no other number needs to move.

issues.claim: founder_md email: "which is still listed as the website on your Lawyers.com profile"; walk-in opener: "while Lawyers.com still lists it as your website"
issues.problem: Overstated. The Lawyers.com page shows no website field for the firm at all today; the old domain appears only under "Additional Links" (confirmed live). audit_md states this correctly, so the owner-facing copy contradicts the audit and the firm could check and dispute it in the first reply.
issues.fix: Use "still listed under Additional Links on your Lawyers.com profile" in the email and "Lawyers.com still lists it under Additional Links" in the opener. Relatedly, step 2's "remove it from the Lawyers.com/Martindale profile" can drop Martindale: the Martindale organization page shows no website field, only the address and practice areas.

issues.claim: audit_md: "The claimed Google profile carries 2 reviews at 3.0"; rescue.json after_fix: "the claimed Google Business Profile"
issues.problem: Ownership/verification status is not stated by any public source I could open. The Maps listing loads with hours, phone and a website link and shows no "Claim this business" prompt, which hints the profile is managed, but that is an inference, not a sourced fact.
issues.fix: Write "the NordLaw Google profile" and, if the point matters, add it to caveats as an inference ("the listing appears to be managed by the firm - no 'claim this business' prompt is shown").

issues.claim: audit_md length: brief requires the body to be at most 300 words
issues.problem: The body runs to about 312 words excluding the H1 title (about 323 including it), so it is slightly over the limit.
issues.fix: Cut roughly 15-20 words: shorten the parenthetical hours in steps 2-4 and tighten the closing paragraph (e.g. "Ask for a review at the end of each matter").
